tier_reason: Tier raised from B on the same evidence, for consistency with the luajit/luajit, pypy/pypy and cisco/chezscheme entries tiered A on this harness: kostya/benchmarks (independent, README updated 2026-07-19) publishes the code (brainfuck/bf.lua and primes/primes.lua vs brainfuck/bf3.py and primes/primes.py), the run commands (common/commands.mk LUA_RUN `lua` and PYTHON3_RUN `python3`), the Debian-packaged interpreters (docker/Dockerfile), the versions (docker/versions.rb records `lua -v` = 5.4.7 and Python 3.14.6) and the CPU (Intel Xeon E-2324G). All README numbers match the Lua, Python, Ruby, Tcl, Perl, PHP and Lua/luajit rows exactly.

corrections.claimed_speedup: kostya/benchmarks median wall time (lower is better). Brainfuck bench.b: Lua 37.051 s vs Python 61.009 s (about 1.65x less time, derived from page data), Ruby 74.107 s, Tcl (FP) 189.615 s, Perl 225.517 s; Lua also uses the least memory of these (2.62 MiB base RSS vs 11.38 MiB for Python) and less energy (1528.23 J vs 2601.10 J). Primes: Lua 1.056 s vs Python 1.725 s (about 1.63x, derived from page data) and Ruby 1.794 s. Faster than Lua: PHP 34.055 s and Ruby (--jit) 30.807 s on bench.b, Ruby/truffleruby 0.871 s on Primes, and Lua/luajit (5.686 s, 0.309 s) and Python/pypy (9.398 s, 0.617 s) on both.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Interpreters are Debian forky packages installed in docker/Dockerfile and run as `lua file.lua` and `python3 file.py` (common/commands.mk); distro build flags are not stated. The README version table is generated by docker/versions.rb from `lua -v`, the same `lua` command the harness runs, and reports Lua 5.4.7 (Python 3.14.6), while docker/Dockerfile at HEAD lists the lua5.5 and liblua5.5-dev packages, so the binary behind `lua` is most likely 5.4.7 but not certain.
corrections.caveats: Lua is the embedded-scripting category's own named baseline (spec Part 4: Lua, Duktape, QuickJS), so this record is evidence about the incumbent rather than an alternative to it; the only useful comparison here is against other general scripting languages (CPython, Ruby, Perl, Tcl), none of which is a category baseline. Plain Lua has rows in only two of the shootout's six suites (bench.b and Primes); mandel.b, Base64, Json and Matmul have no plain Lua row. PHP 8.4 and Ruby with --jit beat Lua on bench.b, TruffleRuby beats it on Primes. One author wrote all the tests, so ports may differ in idiom, and the timings are single medians on one machine. The README version table (Lua 5.4.7, from `lua -v` in docker/versions.rb) and the Dockerfile's lua5.5 package disagree, so the exact interpreter timed is not certain. The GitHub repository is a development mirror updated irregularly (pull requests not accepted); it has no LICENSE file, and the MIT licence text is in the copyright notice at the end of lua.h. www.lua.org was not opened.

notes: Numbers verified row by row in kostya/benchmarks README; tier raised B to A to match the LuaJIT, PyPy and Chez Scheme entries from the same harness. Lua is the category's own baseline: per the boostorg/geometry, flame/blis, brotli and XNNPACK precedent the orchestrator may fold it as a duplicate of the incumbent, although QuickJS (also a named baseline) was kept in this wave. Metadata confirmed: 10.4k stars, last commit 2026-09-16, MIT via lua.h notice.

tier_reason: The numbers are real medians in ThePhD/lua-bindings-shootout benchmark_results/lua_bindings_shootout.json, measured by a third party, but the harness is obscure (14 stars, run by the author of the competing sol2), the CPU model and compiler version are not stated in the repo (8 logical CPUs at 2592 MHz, Windows x64 release build, 2018-09-28), and LuaBridge is pulled from an unpinned shallow clone of master (cmake/Modules/FindLuaBridgeDev.cmake), so it falls short of a well-known independent suite. The win over the chosen baseline (luabind) is mixed and the record omitted two of its losses.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Median cpu_time in ns from the shootout JSON (lower is better), LuaBridge vs luabind on the 13 shared rows: faster on 8, table_get 102.5 vs 224.6 (about 2.2x), table_global_string_get 112.3 vs 199.5 (1.8x), table_global_string_set 15.7 vs 110.9 (7.1x), optional_failure 22.5 vs 147.5 (6.6x), optional_half_failure 138.1 vs 353.0 (2.6x), optional_success 210.0 vs 360.6 (1.7x), return_userdata 16880.7 vs 20403.0 (1.2x), c_function 2950.6 vs 3442.4 (1.17x); slower on 5, member_function_call 21449.3 vs 15694.7, userdata_variable_access 24414.1 vs 15346.0, table_chained_get 276.2 vs 251.1, c_function_through_lua_in_c 131.1 vs 78.5 and lua_function_in_c 131.8 vs 59.3. Ratios and counts derived from page data. Among all 16 bindings LuaBridge ranks 2nd on optional_failure and 3rd on table_global_string_set, but 15th of 16 on member_function_call, 14th of 14 on lua_function_in_c, 12th of 14 on table_get and c_function_through_lua_in_c, and 9th of 10 on userdata_variable_access (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Windows x64 release build of lua_bindings_shootout.exe (library_build_type release) against PUC-Rio Lua 5.3.4 with Google Benchmark; the repo's CMakeLists sets /std:c++latest for MSVC and no explicit optimization flags; LuaBridge is fetched as a shallow clone of vinniefalco/LuaBridge master with no tag (cmake/Modules/FindLuaBridgeDev.cmake, internal label 1.0.2), so the timed code is the 2018 master, not release 2.10. A WebSearch snippet says Visual Studio 2017 (snippet only).
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1.8k stars, 360 forks; the lua-bindings-shootout harness has 14 stars
corrections.caveats: LuaBridge does not claim to be the fastest: its manual says it 'comes close to the highest possible performance' but 'is not quite the fastest' and that OOLua slightly outperforms it in some tests. The chosen baseline, luabind, is one of the slowest bindings in the shootout and is not a category baseline; against the real floor, the plain Lua C API, LuaBridge is slower on every shared row (c_function 2950.6 vs 2131.0 ns, table_get 102.5 vs 17.6 ns), and it is slower than sol2 and sol3 on most rows, ranking in the lower half of 16 bindings on most tests. Data is from 2018 (Lua 5.3.4, an unpinned 2018 LuaBridge master), the CPU model and compiler version are not stated, and the shootout is run by the author of sol2, a competing library. Several benchmarks have no LuaBridge row (stateful_function_object, multi_return, table_set, table_chained_set). Not a duplicate of LuaBridge3: kunitoki/LuaBridge3 is a fork of this repository, while vinniefalco/LuaBridge remains a separately maintained 2.x line (dmitry-t released 2.10 on 2025-10-13) with its own third-party evidence; LuaBridge3's own README chart shows LuaBridge3 faster than vanilla LuaBridge on 12 of 22 shared cases.

notes: Separate project, not a duplicate of LuaBridge3 (kunitoki/LuaBridge3 is the fork; this upstream 2.x line is still maintained, release 2.10 on 2025-10-13, and the shootout timed this repository's master, not LuaBridge3). Downgraded B to C: obscure 14-star harness from the sol2 author without CPU model or compiler version, unpinned LuaBridge revision, and a mixed 8-wins-5-losses result against luabind, a slow non-incumbent; record two omitted losses and 'slower than the plain Lua C API on every row' as shortcomings. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 1.8k stars, last commit 2025-10-13, active.

tier_reason: The only reachable numbers are a third-party GitHub issue (#4386) that compares JerryScript ESNext with Duktape and QuickJS on the V8 suite but states no hardware, compiler version or memory-measurement method, and its peak-memory figures are implausible as labelled; that is numbers without methodology, tier C. Samsung's first-party SunSpider RSS slides are blocked here (snippet only) and would also be C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Issue #4386 lists 'peak memory consumption' (labelled KB) of 239,664 for JerryScript ESNext vs 582,240 for Duktape and 5,523,792 for QuickJS (JerryScript about 2.4x less than Duktape, derived from page data). On speed JerryScript loses on every test: V8 TotalScore 250 vs Duktape 487 and QuickJS 1,042 (higher is better), per test vs Duktape Richards 173 vs 223, DeltaBlue 180 vs 282, Crypto 182 vs 385, RayTrace 291 vs 617, EarleyBoyer 408 vs 686, RegExp 155 vs 221, Splay 365 vs 1296, NavierStokes 398 vs 1073, so about 1.9x slower than Duktape overall (derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: The only numeric comparison reachable is a third-party GitHub issue (#4386, opened 2020-12-29 by lygstate, still open with the discussion label, no replies), not project-authored. It shows JerryScript slower than Duktape on all eight V8 tests and much slower than QuickJS; the claim that holds is memory only (README: 'Heavily optimized for low memory consumption'). The peak-memory row is not credible as labelled: Node.js and Node.js Jitless share the identical 73,873,464 'KB' (about 70 GB) and QuickJS shows 5.5 GB, so the unit or method is wrong (as bytes the figures would be plausible), and no measurement method, hardware or compiler version is given. The JerryScript build used --system-allocator=ON (malloc instead of its compact heap), --cpointer-32bit=ON, --jerry-debugger=ON and --lto=OFF, so neither its memory nor its speed reflects a footprint-tuned build. Counter-evidence from the independent ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark CI (V8 v7 suite, 10/5/2026): JerryScript 3.0.0 completes only Richards, DeltaBlue, Crypto and RayTrace (no total score) and is slower than Duktape 2.99.99 on all four on ubuntu (273/276/301/344 vs 288/315/783/584) and macos-arm64 (205/229/261/337 vs 538/632/1257/1032), and its executable is larger there (454.2K vs 370.4K on ubuntu); build configurations differ. Samsung's first-party slides (SunSpider 1.0.2 max RSS on Raspberry Pi 2, JerryScript 1.0 vs Duktape 1.5.1) report lower RSS for JerryScript, e.g. 3d-cube 35 vs 125 KB, 3d-raytrace 185 vs 339 KB, access-binary-trees 38 vs 160 KB, crypto-md5 142 vs 261 KB, but slideshare and summit.riot-os.org were blocked, so these come from a search snippet only. Last commit 2025-10-08 is one day inside the 12-month active window (the previous commit was 2025-06-03), so it turns stale on 2026-10-09.

notes: Issue #4386 numbers match the record; tier C stands (third-party, no methodology). Record as shortcomings: slower than Duktape on all eight V8 tests (250 vs 487), peak-memory figures implausible as labelled with no method, JerryScript built with system allocator and debugger, independent ahaoboy CI shows JerryScript 3.0.0 failing half the V8 suite and slower than Duktape on the rest; memory win corroborated only by Samsung's first-party slides (snippet only). Metadata confirmed: Apache-2.0, 7.4k stars, last commit 2025-10-08 (active by one day).
